The symptoms of someone never content with their portion. And I try to make myself feel above/better than her for it.

There's a fantasy here, a desire to show her something better. Like saying "come with me, bring your art supplies," and we go into the city and she paints and I write music. And in doing so, she feels connected to me. It's like there are competing interests. On one side, the virtuous, I want to help. Despite any emotions, any pain she may cause, I want to give her this gift of experience. To show that it's possible to be free, to smile, to be happy. To kick back and do nothing. And in this fantasy, I see myself as The Sage, giving a gift of freedom. We sit in silence and embrace the purity. Then the other is the lustful. Such an opportunity would, in my past, completely be used to create romantic opportunities. From that perspective, I've never realized how much in the past I'd done so, and it makes sense why I'd see it as so corrupting. I set up many of these "dates" with Jess, we went out hiking and talking about life and music and everything. It didn't feel like it because we were friends hanging out. but now, that sort of thing feels like it's a corruption. It's funny, I see now the Self 1 sabotage, because in the past I never thought about it. But putting it on the spot, it seems so complicated. I don't feel like I'm allowed to access that virtuous side around her, which is what makes it so painful. What makes me feel so conflicted is the ethicsi draw from. They talk of treating everyone this way, but would I do this with Devor? Kevin? Momo? If not, then why for her? And I feel like the only resolution I could come to is lust. It makes me sad that the only thing currently energizing me to do such a thing is lust, but even sadder that I wouldn't just do it with friends to have a creative time at the park.

The fantasy is still true, even if not with her.

It wasn't really about her at all. It was that I really struggled to represent the person I wanted to be in that conversation. I didn't really have words to articulate the kind of relationship I want to have, the kind of person I want to be with, and I think her saying I was picky or particular hurt me. But more than anything she could've said, I think what was hard was thinking that she could've been right about a lot of it. I think I still place an inordinate value on superficial qualities, and I worry about falling into a relationship again with someone that hurts me. And it's like...in fairly certain I wouldn't, because I'm not doing it with the people in my life now. But some part of me wants to prove Mimza wrong, and I think the part of me that's attracted to her is only that way either superficially or just to prove to myself that I could save her. Beyond that, I hate the idea that she might see me as superficial and egotistical. Like that's usually what offends me the most. Like she talks about the ego on drummers or superficiality or objectification, slinging these things around as if everyone is doing it. And it hurts when she says those things about me because I've tried so hard to stay away from it. But there's truth to it, I still feel super attracted to a lot  of superficial things. I've tried to be generous. When I hear myself talk about what I want though, it feels fake. To say I want someone to give flowers to, to dance in the kitchen with, to write songs with, or cook with, to go on adventures with, etc, that feels real. But for some reason when I talk with them about it, it feels like a white knight version. Someone to buy flowers for and treat well and compliment and whatever else. I want someone to share a life with, and I think the part I fail to mention is that I have to be with someone that I feel deserves that. The part I struggle mentioning is how I'm not a short term kinda guy, I don't play games with my heart, and I just want someone who's able to prove to me they're capable of listening and growing.

It's something that Adlerian psychology has opened my eyes too much more. Even with that, there's a give and take which goes for everyone. It feels like my favorite people already get that. I tolerate it because I work with her, but I'm really not a fan of her and it feels bad to say it. But I don't like who I become around her, or the way she makes me feel

"In reality, to achieve such an ordered mental condition is not as easy as it sounds. Contrary to what we tend to assume, the normal state of the mind is chaos. Without training, and without an object in the external world that demands attention, people are unable to focus their thoughts for more than a few minutes at a time. It is relatively easy to concentrate when attention is structured by outside stimuli, such as when a movie is playing on the screen, or when while driving heavy traffic is encountered on the road. If one is reading an exciting book, the same thing occurs, but most readers still begin to lose concentration after a few pages, and their minds wander away from the plot. At that point, if they wish to continue reading, they must make an effort to force their attention back to the page.
We don't usually notice how little control we have over the mind, because habits channel psychic energy so well that thoughts seem to follow each other by themselves without a hitch. After sleeping we regain consciousness in the morning when the alarm rings, and then walk to the bathroom and brush our teeth. The social roles culture prescribes then take care of shaping our minds for us, and we generally place ourselves on automatic pilot till the end of the day, when it is time again to lose consciousness in sleep. But when we are left alone, with no demands on attention, the basic disorder of the mind reveals itself.
With nothing to do, it begins to follow random patterns, usually stopping to consider something painful or disturbing. Unless a person knows how to give order to his or her thoughts, attention will be attracted to whatever is most problematic at the moment: it will focus on some real or imaginary pain, on recent grudges or long-term frustrations. Entropy is the normal state of consciousness-a condition that is neither useful
nor enjoyable." - Flow 119

I've been thinking a lot about contentment with your slice of the pie. Like at work, we split a pumpkin loaf 5 ways for 5 people. One person didn't want their slice. I think self sacrifice would mean giving away your slice when you do want it. Greed would be taking someone else's slice. Generosity on the other hand would be offering the extra slice even if you might want it. Likewise, temperance is recognizing you might not need two slices. Contentment with your portion means that even if you have an extra slice, you're content with just the one. You can still want more, but you don't need it. I feel like there's a better way to formulate all this, but it's not a bad example.

But in the vein of society, I think contentment with your portion means finding joy no matter what you make. Like if I'm a doctor, my portion (financially) endows different privileges than a part time grocery store clerk. Contentment is living well within each portion respectively. Both contribute to society in different ways. You can still strive for more, to do better, but...this is where I get confused

What I notice with my family and Erick is when you lead with generosity, others do the same. Yesterday, my dad threw my clothes in the dryer. My mom cleaned the kitchen after me. I emptied the dishwasher. This morning, Erick was always a step ahead of me, and I did my best to mirror this. Generosity in this regards feels like tapping in to the unlimited potential of working together. We become appendages of the same body, but only when we ourselves are taken care of.

Generous people rush to the aid of other generous people. With that, it becomes all the more obvious when the pursuit is self-serving rather than a commitment to the whole. Everyone feels it without having to explain it
